findings.description: The worker seams read task+ctrl RPC [38,12,13,1] and events+mgmt RPC [18,12,15,1]. These preserve task/control and events/management shorthand and two opposite arrows, but neither states gRPC. RPC does not uniquely identify gRPC. The source fixed constraint explicitly contrasts worker gRPC with filesystem HTTP over Unix-domain sockets; generator prose cannot supply the missing on-view protocol specificity.

runtime → daemon reads HTTP over UDS [42,20,13,1], not filesystem HTTP over UDS. Protocol and transport survive but the filesystem purpose/qualifier is absent. A separate Filesystem + volumes node cannot implicitly restore that label on a different route.

backend → container reads runs process [11,36,12,1], omitting the source-required user qualifier. The generator explicitly dropped user to clear an ownership warning in v1-a. The source differentiates a user process from an arbitrary runtime/service process; documented abbreviation and an attempt budget do not authorize losing that meaning.

The floating palette overwrites Task container at [10,41] and [10,42] (request's zero-based (9,40)/(9,41)). The node loses its lower left side cell and bottom-left corner; those cells use palette RGB (168,153,104), not node RGB (226,156,175), or selected RGB (216,166,87). Known observed defect fails border_integrity and layout_fit. Seven of eight boxes remain intact; 8/8 selected occurrences does not mean 8/8 complete selected borders.

Dots obscure corner glyphs on 6 routes in 28 route-frame observations. e2 hits [33,16] at frames 0/1/18/19 and [33,8] at 16/17; e3 hits ╮ [37,21] at 2/3/6/7/10/11/14/15/18/19; e5 hits [37,28] at 0/1; e6 hits [32,29] at 14/15; e7 hits [11,37] at 4/5/10/11/16/17; e8 hits [39,37] at 14/15. Thus the acknowledged e3 issue is broader than the generator report, and check's 0 violations is contradicted. Frame 0 is partial but all its dots are visible; 26 of the 28 hits occur in complete frames. Observed animation defect, not a capability/evidence blocker or a synchronized-arrival issue.

Shared update cadence does not equal shared cells-per-time speed: between complete frames 1 (100 ms) and 2 (200 ms), e1 [36,12]→[36,13], e2 [33,16]→[33,15], and e5 [37,28]→[36,28] move one route cell; e3 [36,20]→[37,21], e4 [38,20]→[39,21], e6 [39,28]→[38,29], e7 [9,36]→[10,37], and e8 [32,36]→[33,37] move two route cells. No wrap occurs on that transition. The common nominal 0.5 setting and paired static frames cannot prove equal geometric travel. This is a constant-speed quality defect, not a failure for long routes finishing later.
